groups.keep: Kept: a business problem a website can solve, an economic lane that can pay for it, and a concept that shows the fix.
groups.solved: Archived: their own route already works, or is being replaced. The concept restyles it; it doesn't solve a business problem.
groups.low-ticket: Archived: walk-in or low-ticket trade. The July audit's ROI map puts it in the lean-presence lane, where a bespoke site doesn't pay back.
groups.not-local: Archived: the website decision sits with a group, brand or head office, not the door we would walk into.
groups.relationship: Archived: demand arrives by referral, regulation, waiting list or habit. A website is not the lever.
groups.unverified: Archived: trading status or site state isn't confirmed well enough to pitch.
groups.overlap: Archived: a real case, but the kept list already carries this shape and town.

concepts.reason: c.2012 ASP.NET template with 2013 UTM tags in front of a working Bookin1 engine. Highest-value room in either town; the most developed concept (10 routes).
A venue that sells dates, with no enquiry form, no date capture and no availability check; every wedding lead has to be a phone call. The concept adds the date-and-guests enquiry.
Kept as Hugh McCann's sister property: a hibu legacy brochure with no prominent direct booking, flagged by the July audit. One family, one conversation, two sites. Unpublished concept.

Named by the July audit as an immediate direct-booking prospect: rooms sold only through Booking.com / Airbnb and the phone; own domain is a parked frameset. Our own brief warns the house may not miss a site, and that's the first thing to test.
Nine named rooms and a £80–£120 rate card, but 'Book Now' is an Elementor contact form whose button reads 'Sumbit'. Gallery is one 2019 shoot. Visitors who want to book leave for an OTA.
Named by the July audit as an immediate prospect. Supper clubs sell through Facebook / Instagram only; logged out, the next date is unreachable. One-sheet is built and its QR chain is verified.

Trek dealer and Cyclescheme retailer since 2002 on a free-tier 2014 Wix site with no range, prices or booking. Workshop booking and Cycle to Work are measurable actions; the concept is a six-page site.
2017 Divi build that blocks zoom; 'Book Appointments' is a phone number and an email; the census domain is dead. Appointment requests are the measurable action. Already the homepage's worked example.

Both practice domains hand patients over plain HTTP to another practice's page, including the domain in the practice's own email address. The only case with a privacy dimension. Ownership by DJ Maguire Dental Group is unestablished and must be settled first.

The July audit put it in 'repair before rebuild': opening status and party terms are pushed to Facebook, whose hours widget was 'updated about 5 years ago'. Parties (£12.50–£13.50 a head, £100 minimum, per its own site) are the measurable action.
No website, just a Gmail address and social. The July audit's best shared-platform case. Kept as a channel to every member business rather than as revenue; volunteer committee.
Replied 27 July 2026: a new website is already built and will launch with the accommodation. No current opportunity.
Sister business to The Buck's Head, whose owners have already told us a new site is built. Pitching the sister is pitching the same people.
New official site (thedonard.co.uk) with its own identity, rates and booking engine, found on build day. The concept is a feature proposal to a hotel that just rebuilt.
Maintained GuestDiary site with real availability search. The concept is a journey tweak, not a problem the Inn has told anyone it has.
Working Shopify store with checkout and current listings. The case was first-screen calm, which is a preference, not a business problem.
The July audit's 'leading' independent-retail site. The reviewer recommended stopping it on 3 August; the concept can't show a single artwork.
Case-study premise was found false on 3 August; the live portfolio is a photographed grid. A contractor since 1973 wins work by tender and relationship, not by a filterable register.
Booksy diary already takes bookings. The concept is continuity copy around a working engine.
Two-site group (Newcastle + Belfast) with a WordPress site and ResDiary booking.
Live transactional WordPress / WooCommerce site with 2025 content. A stale footer year is not a business case.
Shopify store taking UK and Ireland orders, 764 reviews claimed. The concept restyles a working shop.
Rebuilt its site in 2025/26. Three rooms; a booking engine is the only gap, and they have just chosen not to buy one.
Live Squarespace portfolio-and-enquiry site. The concept adds a 'systems selector'; the business already has the lead route that matters.
Clubforce renewals and Koalander court booking already run membership. Volunteer club with no budget line for this.
Catalogue site and busy Facebook already work hard, by our own brief's reading.
Live Squarespace site with menus and booking. Unpublished concept.
Live Squarespace site with menus. Concept uses a generic drawn shopfront. Unpublished.
Current Duda site (© 2026). Placeholder before; boilerplate case study.
Live Squarespace site with contact and Instagram. Workshop booking could be a lever, but the business already has an owned route.
Own site plus Blackcircles tyre booking already take the job. Unpublished.
Live WordPress site; hire booked by appointment, which works. Fashion boutique is a medium-ROI lane.
Own site and Facebook already carry the room; phone is the booking path. The concept is a promenade-first restyle with no new action.
Two-year-old walk-in café, social only. Lovely bilingual concept, but it's the audit's lowest ROI lane. Also the one failing test in the 27 Sept baseline.
Seasonal arcade: the audit's 'one live information page plus Google' lane.
Walk-in café with 8.3K followers and an ice-cream group behind it. Needs a Google Business Profile website field, not a bespoke site.
Walk-in coffee shop. Hero restyle; no customer action beyond walking in.
Walk-in brunch café, Instagram only. Lean-presence lane.
Walk-in café; no official website or social confirmed. Lean-presence lane.
Walk-in coffee bar. Lean-presence lane.
Heritage sweet shop; walk-in, low ticket.
Walk-in diner. Platter catering is the one lever, and it's a phone call.
Walk-in café with its own site already (savoy.cafe).
Seasonal promenade juice bar; trading unconfirmed.
Chip shop; trading unconfirmed and the address is in dispute. Takeaways need ordering, not a hero.
High-street butcher; walk-in. Lean-presence lane.
Shopping-centre butcher and carvery; walk-in.
Walk-in bakery. The mail-order mixes are the one lever, and they're unverified.
Toy shop; walk-in; trading unconfirmed.
Promenade joke shop with its own site already. Generic drawn shopfront. Unpublished.
Vintage shop; social only; trading unconfirmed.
Salon; bookings by phone. Low ticket, repeat trade that's already loyal.
Residential salon with its own site. Generic drawn shopfront. Unpublished.
Florist built from directory listings only. Unpublished.
Taxi dispatch: people ring the number they already have.
The audit found live Lorem ipsum on its store. That's a one-hour repair to mention in person, not a redesign. Generic drawn shopfront. Unpublished.
concepts.reopen: Offer the Lorem ipsum fix as a free presence-repair favour if we are ever in the shop.

concepts.reason: Real gap (no named product or price), but it's a micro-producer and the concept can only show placeholders.
Travelling party business on Wix and a Facebook diary that works for it.
Facebook only, and search is swamped by Newcastle-upon-Tyne. That's a real findability problem, but a presence-repair one: a Google profile and one page.
concepts.reopen: Once a presence-repair package exists, this is its first local test.

concepts.reason: Branch of a 53-pharmacy group; the website decision is made at group level. Unpublished.
National brand with its own site. Recorded as a chain / brand in the census.
Belfast-and-Dundrum group; the July audit rated its platform 'strong'. Unpublished.
One house of a multi-centre day-care organisation with its own site. Unpublished.
Sole-practitioner solicitor on a 2013 site. Clients come by referral; a restyle doesn't change that.
Two-solicitor firm listed in the regulated directory. Referral trade; one-page concept.
Funeral director chosen by reputation and family history. Sensitive to pitch; trading unconfirmed.
Day nursery since 2004. Places fill by word of mouth and waiting list.
Sole physiotherapist with her own site; referral trade. Unpublished.
Genuinely without a website, but the eye-test diary is recall and habit, and audiology booking runs through a partner.
concepts.reopen: Its shop refit is a natural relaunch moment. Look again when the builders are out.

concepts.reason: Commercial-vehicle and car workshop; trade customers ring. Trading unconfirmed.
Held since July: trading unconfirmed. A paid Wix domain that has never shown a page.
concepts.reopen: Confirm trading at the yard. If open, heating-oil season (October–February) makes an order-a-fill page timely.

concepts.reason: Trading unconfirmed; listed domain returns 410.
Site returned HTTP 500 on the only check; state unconfirmed.
concepts.reopen: Holiday-home sales and pitch fees are high value. Re-probe; if the site is still down, it's a strong dead-site case.

concepts.reason: Domain doesn't resolve and the Used Cars NI profile showed 'No cars found'. A dead site can mean a business winding down sales.
concepts.reopen: Confirm they still sell cars. If so, it's the clearest 'your site is gone' conversation we have.

concepts.reason: A real case (72 beds, group bookings, broken HTTPS), but the kept list already holds three Newcastle / Dundrum accommodation cases.
concepts.reopen: First replication target if an accommodation pilot works.
